findings.title: Corrosion visible along driver-side rocker panel
findings.detail: A band of corrosion is visible along the lower rocker panel, roughly one third of the panel length. The texture in this image is consistent with surface corrosion rather than perforation, but whether the metal is compromised underneath cannot be determined from a photograph.
findings.confidenceBasis: The region is well lit and unobstructed. Confidence is held below 0.8 because surface corrosion and early perforation look similar at this resolution.

evidence.caption: Corrosion band along the lower rocker panel

findings.sellerQuestion: How long has the rust on the rocker panel been there, and has any bodywork been done to it?
findings.mechanicCheck: Ask a mechanic to probe the rocker panel and inspect the seam from underneath on a lift.

findings.title: Deformation on rear quarter panel
findings.detail: A shallow deformation is visible on the rear quarter panel above the wheel arch. No paint fracture is visible at this resolution.
findings.confidenceBasis: The shading pattern is consistent with a dent, but a reflection or a shadow can produce a similar pattern. Confidence held low.

evidence.caption: Deformation above the rear wheel arch

findings.sellerQuestion: Do you know how the dent on the rear quarter happened?

findings.title: Driver seat bolster wear
findings.detail: Wear is visible on the outer driver seat bolster, consistent with regular entry and exit over time. No tearing is visible.
findings.confidenceBasis: Bolster wear is one of the more reliably visible interior signals in a well-lit cabin photo.

findings.title: Check-engine lamp illuminated in the instrument cluster
findings.detail: A check-engine lamp is illuminated in the cluster in this photograph. What triggered it cannot be determined without reading the fault codes with a scan tool.
findings.confidenceBasis: The lamp shape and position are clearly legible. The reading is about the photograph, not about the vehicle's condition.

evidence.caption: Illuminated lamp in the instrument cluster

findings.sellerQuestion: The check-engine light is on in your photo. What code is it throwing, and how long has it been on?
findings.mechanicCheck: Have the fault codes read with a scan tool before agreeing on a price. A $20 code read can be the difference between a sensor and a catalytic converter.

findings.title: Odometer reads 128,540 miles
findings.detail: The odometer display reads 128,540 miles in this photograph. This matches the mileage stated by the seller. A photograph of an odometer is evidence of what the display showed when the photo was taken, and nothing more.
findings.confidenceBasis: All digits are legible and unobstructed. Confidence reflects the legibility of the display, not the truthfulness of the reading.
findings.sellerQuestion: Can you show me the title and any service records so I can check the mileage history?

findings.title: Front left tread appears low
findings.detail: Tread depth on the front left tire appears low relative to the tread block spacing visible in this image. Tread depth from a photograph is an estimate; a tread gauge costs a few dollars and settles it in seconds.
findings.confidenceBasis: Tread depth from a single photograph at this angle is unreliable. Confidence is low on purpose and this finding should be treated as a prompt to measure, not a measurement.

evidence.caption: Tread block area on the front left tire

findings.sellerQuestion: How old are the tires, and were they all replaced at the same time?
findings.mechanicCheck: Measure tread depth on all four tires with a gauge and check for uneven wear that would suggest an alignment problem.

findings.title: Residue visible on engine bay surface
findings.detail: A dark residue is visible on a surface in the engine bay. Whether this is an active leak, a past leak that was cleaned, or spilled fluid from a top-up cannot be determined from a photograph.
findings.confidenceBasis: The residue is visible but its source is not traceable in a single still image.
findings.sellerQuestion: Is the engine losing any fluid? When were the fluids last topped up or changed?
findings.mechanicCheck: Ask a mechanic to identify the fluid and find its source.

findings.confidenceBasis: Reported directly by NHTSA for this VIN. Not a model judgment.
findings.sellerQuestion: Has recall FIX000002 been performed? A dealer will do it free - ask for the paperwork.
